facts.text: Heavy machines slow using friction brakes called the service brake, a retarder that uses the drivetrain to hold speed on long descents, and, on many machines, a hydrostatic drive that brakes when the operator eases off.
facts.quote: Heavy machines slow down in three ways: with friction brakes (the service brake), with a retarder that uses the drivetrain to hold speed on long descents, and on many machines with a hydrostatic drive that brakes by itself when the operator eases off.

facts.text: The collision system commands the service brake on heavy machines.
facts.quote: It is the brake the collision system commands.

facts.text: ISO 3450 treats service braking, secondary braking as a backup, and parking braking to hold the machine still as separate functions.
facts.quote: The secondary brake is a backup and the parking brake holds the machine still; ISO 3450 treats the three functions separately [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Large haul trucks use the retarder on long haul-road descents to prevent service-brake overheating.
facts.quote: large haul trucks descend long haul roads on the retarder so the service brakes do not overheat.

facts.text: Retarder power is limited, so retarder deceleration decreases as machine speed and mass increase.
facts.quote: Its power is limited, so the deceleration it gives falls as speed and mass rise.

facts.text: The booklet quotes the patent formula a = P / (v x m) - g x sin θ for retarder deceleration, where P is retarding power in watts, v is speed in m/s, m is mass in kg, and the last term represents downhill pull.
facts.quote: The booklet quotes a patent formula for this case, `a = P / (v x m) - g x sin θ`, where P is retarding power in watts, v speed in m/s, m mass in kg and the last term the downhill pull;

facts.text: Historic mining studies reported 1 to 2 seconds of extra lag for retarders.
facts.quote: historic mining studies reported 1 to 2 s of extra lag for retarders [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Some compact machines list hydrostatic dynamic braking as their auxiliary brake.
facts.quote: Some compact machines list this as their auxiliary brake

facts.text: ISO 3450 allows the service-brake function to involve the propel control, but continuous "back throttling" is not a substitute for a parking brake.
facts.quote: ISO 3450 allows the service-brake function to involve the propel control, but continuous "back throttling" is not a substitute for a parking brake [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Hydrostatic braking depends on oil viscosity, pressure, pump speed and displacement, and engine braking torque, so braking changes with temperature and operating state.
facts.quote: How much braking it gives depends on oil viscosity, pressure, pump speed and displacement and engine braking torque, so it changes with temperature and operating state [Chapter 8].

facts.text: On heavy machines, the response from brake command to deceleration blends hydrostatic slowing, driveline effects, friction braking, and anti-lock behavior, and changes with machine state.
facts.quote: On these machines the step from brake command to deceleration is a blend of hydrostatic slowing, driveline effects, friction braking and anti-lock behavior that changes with state.

facts.text: The booklet concludes that a service-brake model ignoring hydrostatic slowing can trigger braking too early or too late.
facts.quote: The booklet concludes that a service-brake model which ignores hydrostatic slowing can trigger too early or too late

facts.text: The booklet concludes that hydrostatic braking capacity must be modeled as a function rather than a constant.
facts.quote: hydrostatic braking capacity must be modeled as a function and not a constant

facts.text: The booklet concludes that friction-brake-dominant machines and hydrostatic or retarder-blended machines belong in different model families.
facts.quote: friction-brake-dominant machines and hydrostatic or retarder-blended machines belong in different model families [Chapter 8].
